evidence.claim: A role provider can replace another provider's credential by first granting a marginally later expiry (becoming lastProvider), then granting a shorter expiry, bypassing the 'new expiry must be later' restriction.
evidence.support_reason: In _grantRole, when status.hasCredential() and lastProvider is still supported, the only guard is `status.lastProvider == msg.sender || newExpiry > oldExpiry` (line 426). After a first grant with newExpiry > oldExpiry, _setCredentialAndEmitAccessGranted (line 469) sets status.lastProvider = msg.sender, so a second grant passes the `status.lastProvider == msg.sender` branch and can set any expiry, including a shorter one. The same logic exists in AccessControlHooks.sol:426.
preconditions: Attacker is an approved role provider (added by borrower via addRoleProvider)
Victim account has an existing credential from another provider with a later expiry
Attacker's provider TTL allows a first grant with expiry > victim's current expiry

missing_evidence.item: Demonstration that a role provider is an untrusted actor under the contest policy, or that the policy's trusted-role list does not cover role providers acting maliciously
missing_evidence.why: The attack requires an approved role provider to act maliciously. The policy lists Borrowers as trusted and states borrowers determine the conditions/policies under which addresses engage as lenders; role providers are borrower-appointed. If role providers are treated as trusted, the path is excluded by the allowed-actor precondition. The policy does not explicitly name role providers, so this is a genuine ambiguity a judge must resolve.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: The policy or judge confirms role providers are not trusted actors (or that a malicious provider is in scope).

missing_evidence.item: Concrete impact of the shortened expiry: what the victim loses (e.g., inability to deposit/withdraw/transfer) and whether it is recoverable
missing_evidence.why: The report asserts a restriction bypass but does not show a material effect. A shorter expiry only matters if it blocks a specific market action; the report gives no scenario, amounts, or state showing harm. Without this, the severity/impact obligation is unsupported.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A step-by-step scenario shows the victim's credential expiring and a concrete blocked action (deposit/withdraw/transfer) with values.
